comment.narrative:
1: “Youth Empowerment Alliance of Incubators” fosters and incubates youth-led entrepreneurship for achieving the SDGs (Incubators and Innovations)
2: Youth Leadership Initiative inspires and engages young people through innovation and localized actions for SDGs (Inspire and Engage)
3: Forums addressing Youth Leadership, Innovation and Entrepreneurship convened to set the agenda for Asia Pacific-wide initiatives on youth accelerating the SDGs (Network and Policy)
4: Research and knowledge exchange Initiative informs new youth entrepreneurship initiatives, including the work of the “Youth Empowerment Alliance of Incubators” (Knowledge)
5: Financial Action Initiative established to ensure financial sustainability of current and new youth empowerment initiatives (Sustainability)

4.2 A report on the state of youth led entrepreneurship, social innovation and leadership in the context of SDGs published by the Youth Alliance - No target was set for the year as per the Project Document

5.2 A youth startup incubator scheme established to support youth entrepreneurs, with special focus given to young women and marginalised youth - Regional Springboard pre-accelerator programme supports 200 young social entrepreneurs

1.1 Youth Alliance meet regularly for knowledge exchange and best practices on startup support - 210 ecosystem stakeholders have joined Youth Empowerment Alliance. 30 representatives of 27 entrepreneurship support organisations participated in the Springboard Amplifier peer-to-peer learning programme to strengthen their capacities to provide better services to youth-led social enterprises.
1.2 % of regional and local partners satisfied with trainings by the Youth Alliance secretariat - Based on the Springboard Amplifier post-programme survey, the participants rated the programme 9.5/10, indicating a high satisfaction rate. Among 15 survey respondents, all (100 percent) agreed that they are more confident to support young entrepreneurs in the future and think the programme helps their organisations to improve services to social entrepreneurs.
1.5 Regional Summits/Forums on Youth entrepreneurship and innovation convened to foster south-south collaboration - Youth Co:Lab Summit was organised in Singapore on 4-7 July 2022, bringing together 260 in-person participants, including young social entrepreneurs, government representatives, private sector partners and other key ecosystem stakeholders. The summit was rated 8.9/10 for the usefulness for participants personal or professional activities among the post-event survey respondents.
2.1 # of young people developing entrepreneurial mindsets through national training programmes - During the 2021-2022 Youth Co:Lab Programme cycle (July 2021-July 2022), 5134 participants attended youth social innovation and entrepreneurship activities at the national level.
2.2 # youth trainers trained to strengthen SDG based entrepreneurship in ther communities - 186 Movers volunteers were trained through a train-the-trainer approach in 2022 to conduct SDG and 21st century skills development workshops
2.3 # number of SDG solutions created by youth - 180 youth-led social enterprise teams from 23 countries and territories strengthened their SDG solutions through the Youth Co:Labs Regional Springboard Plus programme. This includes 230 young social entrepreneurs, of whom 86 are women.
2.4 % of incubator grantees who are successful 6 months after receipt of grants - As of January 2022, 80 percent of the 430 youth-led social enterprises supported at the regional level were still operational. The figure will be updated 6 months after the completion of the 2022 Springboard Plus programme, which ended in July 2022.
3.1 regional policy dialogue on youth innovation and entrepreneurship convened - Youth Co:Lab Summit in Singapore convened government stakeholders to discuss topics around youth social innovation and entrepreneurship. A Strategic Intelligence Hub, which will serve as a nerve centre to build a community of practice around youth entrepreneurship consisting of regional policy and programmatic leaders at the regional, national and sub-national levels was launched at the summit. The Singapore session engaged 14 government representatives in scoping out the vision and governance structure of the Strategic Intelligence Hub and ideate south-south collaboration ideas on youth entrepreneurship policy programming.
3.3. A regional youth summit on entrepreneurship and innovation convened - Youth Co:Lab Summit was organised in Singapore on 4-7 July 2022, bringing together 260 in-person participants, including young social entrepreneurs, government representatives, private sector partners and other key ecosystem stakeholders. The summit was rated 8.9/10 for the usefulness for participants personal or professional activities among the post-event survey respondents.
4.1 Conduct research of existing networks of business incubators in the Asia-Pacific region to be incorporated into the Youth Alliance on a selective basis conducted - No target was set for the year as per the Project Document. State of the Ecosystem for Youth Entrepreneurship studies were conducted in Indonesia and Singapore. These studies identify entry points for strengthening the ecosystem for youth entrepreneurship and included stakeholder mapping analysis.
4.2 A report on the state of youth led entrepreneurship, social innovation and leadership in the context of SDGs published by the Youth Alliance - No target was set for the year as per the Project Document. 4 National Ecosystem studies were conducted. New national State of the Ecosystem for Youth Entrepreneurship studies were conducted in Indonesia and Singapore, and similar studies have been initiated in the Maldives and Pakistan. Youth Co:Labs first national ecosystem youth entrepreneurship ecosystem diagnostic report was published in Bangladesh in 2021.
5.1 Partnership mechanism developed in order to strengthen youth empowerment initiatives - 210 Ecosystem stakeholder have joined Youth Empowerment Alliance, which is projects core partnership mechanism to strengthen youth empowerment initiatives
5.2 A youth startup incubator scheme established to support youth entrepreneurs, with special focus given to young women and marginalised youth - 230 young social entrepreneurs strengthened their entrepreneurial skills through the regional Springboard Plus incubator programme (105 of them are women).
